My mother-in-law cannot speak English well, so I helped her during a phone appointment. I first asked the doctor whether she needed to speak directly to the patient for consent. Dr Nwufoh responded rudely, saying, “Well, has she given you consent to talk?” When I confirmed that consent had been given, she replied abruptly, “Okay, go on then.”

I explained that I had a few health concerns and began describing that my mother-in-law had brain surgery in 2023 and, over the past week, had been experiencing severe headaches and facial puffiness. The doctor repeatedly interrupted me, saying, “You said you had a few queries, so tell me,” forcing me to repeat myself three times.

I also asked whether my mother-in-law should continue taking certain medications. Dr Nwufoh rushed through the medication list in a rude and dismissive manner. When I explained that I am not a doctor and needed to repeat the medication names I had in front of me to be sure, she sighed audibly and acted as though helping was an inconvenience.

Throughout the call, Dr Nwufoh was extremely rude, abrupt, dismissive, and impatient. There was no sense of concern, empathy, or professionalism particularly worrying given the seriousness of the symptoms following previous brain surgery. I had to push for any action at all, and only after insisting did she agree to a blood test.

At the end of the call, I told her directly that she was being rude and unhelpful and showed no care. Her attitude did not change.

I contacted the receptionist afterward, who provided an email address to make a formal complaint. When I later checked Google reviews, I was concerned to see many similar complaints about this doctor. This raises serious questions about what actions, if any, the GP practice is taking to prevent patients from repeatedly having such negative experiences.

This was a horrible experience with a doctor who showed no compassion, patience, or professionalism. I would not recommend Dr Joy
